L28@P2: The Cross Section Evaluation Working Group is preparing a new ENDF/B release,
L29@P2: ENDF/B-VIII.1. While ENDF/B-VIII.1 is a “minor release” in that it will not include
L30@P2: changes to the Nuclear Data Standards, it is a signficant improvement over previous library
L31@P2: releases. With each release, CSEWG has released a new revision of the ENDF-6 formats
L32@P2: manual. Although ENDF/B-VIII.1 uses the same ENDF-6 format as the previous four library releases (ENDF/B-VIII.0, ENDF/B-VII.1, ENDF/B-VII.0 and ENDF/B-VI), there
L33@P2: have been many corrections and clarifications to the manual as well as a few minor additions
L34@P2: to the ENDF-6 format. These additions include:
L35@P2: • Replaced various synonyms for the 3He nuclide with the word “helion” and the abbreviation “h”.
L36@P2: • Assigned a library identifier (NLIB) for the IAEA Photonuclear Data Library.
L37@P2: • Included graphics to illustrate ENDF-6 sum rules (Sections 0.4.3.11 and 23.2).
L38@P2: • Various background R-matrix options were adopted (Chapter 2)
L39@P2: • Added a generalized information file for MF7 (thermal neutron scattering) files.
L40@P2: Amoung other things, this format allows the evaluator to explicitly state the isotopic
L41@P2: distribution of atoms used in generating the MF7 data so that it can be more easily
L42@P2: linked to a corresponding neutron sub-library evaluation during the processing step
L43@P2: (Chapter 7).
L44@P2: • Added mixed elastic scattering format to File 7 to improve thermal scattering physics
L45@P2: for TSLs containing nuclides with substantial coherent and incoherent scattering cross
L46@P2: sections (Chapter 7).
L47@P2: • Added an option to denote fission as a “decay product” in MF=10 (Chapter 10).
L48@P2: • Equations describing the energies of primary gammas were adjusted to include nuclear
L49@P2: recoil (Chapters 12 and 13).
L50@P2: • Adjusted the procedure for collapsing File 35 covariance data to match those in Files
L51@P2: 31 and 33 (Chapter 35)
L52@P2: • Clarify one of the LTY=0 sub-subsection rule to disallow overlapping NI-typw subsections (Chapter 33)
L53@P2: • Clarified MAT numbers for TSL data (Appendix C)
L54@P2-3: • Various clarifications and minor revisionsIn the early stage of work on the VII-th generation of the library CSEWG made
L55@P3: important decision to use the same formats. This decision was adopted even though it was
L56@P3: argued that it would be timely to modernize the formats and several interesting ideas were
L57@P3: proposed. After careful deliberation CSEWG concluded that actual implementation would
L58@P3: require considerable resources needed to modify processing codes and to guarantee high
L59@P3: quality of the files processed by these codes. The transition to a new format, the Generalized
L60@P3: Nuclear Database Structure (GNDS), is now underway. CSEWG determined that both
L61@P3: ENDF/B-VIII releases will be released in both the ENDF-6 format and in the GNDS format.
L62@P3: Many thanks are due to numerous CSEWG members and international colleagues for
L63@P3: their useful comments and observations on several draft versions. We especially want to
L64@P3: thank all those who provided comments, corrections and format changes on this latest
L65@P3: version of the format manual, in particular B. Beck, J. Brown, C. Chapman, J. Conlin,
L66@P3: D. Cullen, W. Haeck, C. Mattoon, G. Nobre, M. Paris, P. Romano, A. Trkov, D. Wiarda,
L67@P3: and M. Zerkle. We also want to stress that even though the Manual is maintained by the
L68@P3: CSEWG collaboration in the United States, active contribution from the international data
L69@P3: community is essential for achieving its high quality.

L18@P0: We describe the new ENDF/B-VIII.0 evaluated nuclear reaction data library. ENDF/B-VIII.0 fully
L19@P0: incorporates the new IAEA standards, includes improved thermal neutron scattering data and uses
L20@P0: new evaluated data from the CIELO project for neutron reactions on 1H, 16O, 56Fe, 235U, 238U and 239Pu described in companion papers in the present issue of Nuclear Data Sheets. The evaluations
L21@P0: benefit from recent experimental data obtained in the U.S. and Europe, and improvements in theory
L22@P0: and simulation. Notable advances include updated evaluated data for light nuclei, structural materials,
L23@P0: actinides, fission energy release, prompt fission neutron and γ-ray spectra, thermal neutron scattering
L24@P0: data, and charged-particle reactions. Integral validation testing is shown for a wide range of criticality,
L25@P0: reaction rate, and neutron transmission benchmarks. In general, integral validation performance of
L26@P0: the library is improved relative to the previous ENDF/B-VII.1 library.

L165@P2: I. INTRODUCTION
L166@P2: The ENDF library project is coordinated by the
L167@P2: Cross Section Evaluation Working Group (CSEWG) and
L168@P2: CSEWG is releasing the new ENDF/B-VIII.0 library, incorporating work from across the US and the international nuclear science community over the last six years.
L169@P2: The library is being issued in the traditional ENDF-6 format, as well as in an alternative new Generalized Nuclear
L170@P2: Database Structure (GNDS) format.
L171@P2: As was the case for previous ENDF releases [1, 2], the
L172@P2: ENDF/B-VIII.0 library has not been developed in isolation, but rather, it continues to evolve through close
L173@P2: interactions with parallel organizations around the world,
L174@P2: most notably with Europe (JEFF) [3], Japan (JENDL)
